fragments.text: Can you turn the "blocked" into a gantt chart or some other decomposition
b/c just seeing a wall of "blocked" makes it look like everything is  blocked

reply_text:
㊥ (the chart) `progress.py` no longer shows a single "blocked" count. Each blocked row is now placed by where the fix for its blocker stands. 18 of 110 rows compile, and only 16 rows are blocked on something nobody is working on yet:

```
Parse-path curriculum: 18/110 compiled
  ████████▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒░░░░░░░··
    █  18  compiled
    ▓  31  fixed, awaiting re-probe
    ▒  40  fix in progress
    ░  16  fix not started
    ·   5  not probed yet

  blocking causes, by where the fix stands:
   fixed, awaiting re-probe:
     29  m unsolved before Pure   [6af2ff5]
      2  ->.Out                    [73fa028]
   fix in progress:
     34  stuck Decidable (Eq ?m ?m)  [zai-1: Bool-to-Prop discovery]
      6  name not exported           [zai-2: pattern-name lookup; tuple/nomatch, dot-notation queued]
   fix not started:
      5  dependency loader no progress
      4  instance named differently in port
      3  other
      4  four singletons
```

The per-section bars use the same symbols.

🈖 (how a row is placed) Each blocking cause has an entry in a small table at the top of `progress.py`. The entry either names an agent currently working on that cause, or gives the commit that fixes it. The script asks git whether a row's probe ran before that fix commit. If it did, the row counts as "fixed, awaiting re-probe" rather than blocked.

I edit the table by hand when I dispatch a job or merge a fix, so it is only as current as my last edit. I chose this over a true Gantt chart because there are no durations to plot. Probe times are known, but how long a discovery will take isn't.

㊟ (what "fixed, awaiting re-probe" means) Those 31 rows won't all compile on re-probe. Each will move to its next stop, which may be a new cause. A fix moves a row out of that stop, not necessarily all the way to compiled.

(the 6 not-probed rows) Yes, the chart is current. zai-3's sweep has now probed almost everything: 18 of 110 compiled, 87 blocked, and 5 not probed yet (6 a moment ago). zai-3 is still on those last ones. Two causes account for most of the 87 blocked rows:
- 34 rows: stuck `Decidable (Eq ?m ?m)`.
- 29 rows: `m` unsolved before `Pure`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (how current those 29 rows are) All 29 were probed before the fix for that error landed. 25 were probed at `6d6e824` and 4 at `62201b2`. I checked that both are older than `6af2ff5`, the commit that fixes the `m`/`Pure` stop. So those rows record a stop that is already fixed. They won't all compile now; each will show whatever stop comes next.

previous_reply_acts.text: (next step) When zai-3's sweep finishes, I'll have those 29 rows re-probed at the current blank-startup HEAD, `91a6f5b`. That run will show what they are really blocked on now. I'll leave the 34 `Decidable` rows until the Bool-to-Prop fix is in. zai-1 is still running the discovery for it, so re-probing them now would only repeat the known stop.
